answer.why_different: The difference is primarily a different callback address/key, with an additional callback entry. The generated document uses the specification’s notification target name and also adds the corresponding `$request.body` runtime-expression form, while the official document uses `request.body#/notificationRecipientAddress` without the required `$` prefix. However, the generated `{notificationTarget}` key is not itself a valid OpenAPI runtime expression, so the generated side contains an invalid extra callback key.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP mapping specifies that all listed notifications use POST on the resource URI `{notificationTarget}`. The supplied specification evidence does not identify `notificationRecipientAddress` as the callback target.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI 3.0 requires callback keys to be runtime expressions. A request-body expression has the form `$request.body#/...`; therefore `$request.body#/notificationTarget` is structurally valid, whereas `{notificationTarget}` is not shown as a valid runtime expression. The generated side is nevertheless erroneous because it adds the invalid `{notificationTarget}` callback alongside the valid expression rather than providing one valid callback entry.
answer.clearer_why: The generated side makes the intended target property explicit through `$request.body#/notificationTarget`, which is easier to interpret than the official key’s missing `$` prefix and its unsupported `notificationRecipientAddress` name. Its duplicate invalid key does reduce clarity, but the valid generated expression is clearer about the callback address.

##### Runtime Expressions  
Runtime expressions allow defining values based on information that will only be available within the HTTP message in an actual API call.
This mechanism is used by [Link Objects](#link-object) and [Callback Objects](#callback-object).  
The runtime expression is defined by the following [ABNF](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5234) syntax  
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
